title: Worker actions staging enablement and denial proof
goal: Enable worker check-in, check-out, and packet acknowledgement only after reviewed additive SQL, staging feature flag, and scoped denial probes

in: Review and manually apply additive worker-actions SQL to isolated staging.
Enable FEATURE_WORK_MODE_WORKER_ACTIONS only after postflight and denial probes.
out: Automatic migration replay or database reset.
Enabling worker actions before schema and authorization proof.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Reviewed additive SQL is applied one migration at a time with ledger evidence.
Assigned worker check-in/out and acknowledge events persist idempotently.
Unassigned and wrong-tenant actors are denied before mutation.
Worker and manager UI reflect events after reload.

evidence: Wave 34 re-run: 43 test files / 231 tests pass across __tests__/jobs/ + __tests__/hiring/ + __tests__/work-mode/, including the 15 worker-action and manager-attendance assertions in the work-mode API and manager-attendance suites.

Staged and fail-closed, confirmed by reading app/api/work-mode/assignments/[id]/actions/route.ts: both GET and POST check `process.env.FEATURE_WORK_MODE_WORKER_ACTIONS !== '1'` as their first statement and return 503 { code: 'unavailable' } before any client is constructed; the suite asserts createClient was never called on that path. FEATURE_WORK_MODE_WORKER_ACTIONS remains unset.

No service-role privilege on the worker mutation path: the action route uses the request-scoped createClient() only, so check-in/out and acknowledgement writes are subject to RLS as the signed-in worker. The manager attendance read is the only privileged path and it is gated on workforce.view plus revalidated organization/event access.

Authorization precedes mutation: the assignment is resolved from the caller's own read model (404 outside it), then the per-assignment permissions.check_in_out capability is checked (403 when absent), and only then does the insert run. Idempotent replay is limited to the same request id + same action + same assignment, and a request id reused for a different action or packet is rejected.

Type-surface blocker, not an auth blocker: work_mode_check_in_events and work_mode_publication_acknowledgements are created by the active chain (20260922155356_worker_actions_scope_reconciliation.sql) but are absent from lib/database.types.ts, so both the action route and the history read model reach them through documented local any-escapes. They are the only two chain-created relations missing from the generated contract in the whole DB-008 inventory. Handed off to the database lane as HF-WORK-034-WORKER-ACTIONS-TYPE-SURFACE.
No hosted SQL was applied, no feature flag was enabled, no database was reset, and no actor was run.
Transferred from the v1 task; this gate does not keep a locally complete domain implementation active.

progress.summary: Worker and manager attendance contracts re-verified in Wave 34 and still staged and fail-closed. Authorization is server-side and ordered before every mutation, the worker path never uses a service-role client, and the feature flag stays unset so nothing is reachable until the reviewed SQL is proven hosted. All four acceptance criteria require hosted evidence (applied migration ledger, persisted idempotency, wrong-tenant denial probes, reload-visible UI), so the task stays active. The new finding is a generated-contract gap that blocks nothing operationally but does block typed access to the two worker-actions relations.

checkpoints.summary: Denial proof re-verified locally and kept staged and fail-closed; no hosted action taken. Confirmed by reading the code and re-running the suites: the flag gate is the first statement in both handlers, so with FEATURE_WORK_MODE_WORKER_ACTIONS unset the route returns 503 with code unavailable and never constructs a Supabase client at all, which the suite asserts directly; the worker action route uses the request-scoped createClient only and never a service-role client, so every worker mutation stays inside RLS; and authorization runs before any write - the assignment is resolved from the caller's own read model (404), then the per-assignment capability is checked (403), and only then does the insert happen. Idempotent replay and request-id reuse across a different action or packet are already rejected. The one new durable fact is a type-surface blocker, not an auth blocker: work_mode_check_in_events is created by the active chain but missing from the generated contract, so the reads reach it through a documented local any-escape.
next_steps: Hold FEATURE_WORK_MODE_WORKER_ACTIONS off until the database lane reconciles the worker-actions relations and DB-010 supplies hosted postflight plus exact-SHA persona denial probes; then enable on isolated staging only and rerun the worker/manager/wrong-tenant actors.
